steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease muffin cups or line with paper muffin liners.

Sift flour, cornmeal, brown sugar, salt and baking powder together into a large bowl. Dredge the blueberries in the sifted ingredients. In a small bowl, combine the milk, butter and egg. Stir the wet ingredients into the flour mixture just until moistened. Spoon batter into prepared muffin tins.
Bake in preheated oven for 20 minutes. Let muffins sit for 10 minutes before removing from the pan.

raw_recipe.headline: Blueberry Cornmeal Muffins
raw_recipe.description: Blueberry muffins with the hearty flavor of cornmeal. Moist, rich, and heavenly! I'm happy to share my recipe with you.
raw_recipe.name: Blueberry Cornmeal Muffins

review.reviewBody: An Added Note: Fresh blueberries can be used instead of frozen if you like. Also, lately I've been adding an extra 1/2 cup of blueberries which just makes them more heavenly! Hope you enjoy my recipe. - Shelley Albeluhn :o)

I really like this recipe and have been using for years. As others have noted, it does allow for a bit of flexibility (although as written has always worked well for me too). Most recently, I did the following and they were perfect:
-soaked cornmeal in the milk while warming up oven/ preparing other ingredients (approx 15 min), added egg and veg oil (no butter) to milk mixture before mixing wet with combined dry ingredients 
- used 1/2 cup of whole wheat flour and rest (3/4 cup) white
- extra 1/2 cup of blueberries
- baked at 10 min 375* (note that type of pan makes a difference and nonstick/dark pans cook quicker than light), then dropped to 350* for another approx 15 min til golden brown on edges and toothpick inserted came out clean 

Absolutely tender and perfect. The oil gave a lighter texture to the muffins and we ate almost the whole tray in one sitting.

These were very comforting and delicious with a cup of tea. I added 1/3 cup crushed walnuts, and used 1/4 cup milk and 1/4 cup sour cream for the liquid. As to the frozen blueberries, I tossed them with a shake of cinnamon, a tablespoon of sugar and 2 T flour. I also used half white sugar and half brown for the main dough. Lastly I sprinkled a little sugar on the top. Next time I'll crush some walnuts as well for the topping. The dough will be stiff, so I used a rubber frosting "spatula" so as not to crush the blueberries. Excellent recipe. As you can see I played with it a bit and it was very forgiving : )

For years, I kept a cobbler recipe taped to my kitchen cabinet door that I used as a base for multiple quick breads. I lost it in two moves and just remembered some measurements vaguely. This recipe is the one! I didn’t bother with muffin cups, just made it in a pan. Some slight differences: 1 C white whole wheat, 3/4 C cornmeal, buttermilk (actually kefir) instead of milk, half baking powder and half soda, and soaking cornmeal in the milk and egg for 15 - 20 minutes before mixing. It seems like a lot of changes, but it isn’t really. For cobbler, just put the fruit on the bottom. Good for pancakes, shortbread bread for strawberries, and all kinds of other fruits in the batter. YUM.

Would definitely make it again. Reduced the milk to 1/2 cup and added 6 oz plain whole yogurt and a splash of vanilla with the eggs. I used frozen blueberries and rolled them in cornstarch before adding them to the batter. Came out fantastic!

Not a bad recipe, especially if you customize it to your palate. I added about 1 T of orange rind, 1/3 C chopped almonds, 1 t vanilla extract, 1 t cinnamon, split the flour so that it was half AP and half WW and used canola oil. 

A few people noted that this is a very mushy batter so I tried a few things extra to make my muffins turn out well. First I added about 1/3 C of rolled oats to the batter and then I let it all sit for 10 min before portioning it out into the muffin pan. I baked the muffins for 22 min. The muffins turned out nicely and smell/taste great. I really like the cornmeal for making a crumbly texture.
Half the butter and used frozen blueberries. Added 1/2 batter, top blueberries last cover with some batter then bake.

Wow.I tried these because I have too many blueberries & "the boy" likes cornbread.I was a little nervous about it being "cornbread with blueberries" - not so interesting - but it isn't "cornbread with blueberries"!It's lighter (cupcake-ish) & yum!I doubled the recipe.I subbed half cup whole wheat flour, since I'm a sneaky mom, & fresh blueberries.Two cups is the perfect amount of blueberries, btw.I reduced the butter to 3/4c without any problems - may even try 2/3c next time.'Think I'll try less sugar, too; but the full amount isn't insane.It's just me, not you. :D I was anxious over them being so full, but they didn't overflow or even stick to the pan.How cool is that?!?Thanks, Shelley!Oh, & done in exactly 20 minutes! My crew loved them. I used two cups of frozen blueberries, used two eggs instead of one, and lowered the milk to about 7/8 cup because I like a dense, moist muffin texture. The sugar was dark brown, and I sprinkled a little on the tops before baking. Delicious! I'll be making these again.

I've made these quite a few times now and they are always a big hit. I use frozen mixed berries instead of just blueberries and I use silcon muffin cups so they don't stick. I melt the butter in a cup in the microwave and then mix the milk and egg right into the same cup. Instead of mixing the berries into the flour, I put a tablespoon of batter in each cup and then add berries to each so that I can distribute the berries evenly. I then cover them up with the rest of the batter. Everyone who has tried these loves them and they are super easy to make.
Blueberry Cornmeal Muffins by Shelley Albeluhn. Light & delicious. Dbl recipe: decreased butter to 2/3c & sugar to 3/4c; 2c blues is perfect.
Moist, tasty..delicious
I made these for breakfast, using 1 1/4 cups fresh blueberries. Great recipe. The amount of sugar was perfect and the muffins weren't overly sweet.

Truly delicious, just as everyone has said. I also put a lot more blueberries than the recipe called for. I thought about adding a little honey to my second batch, but my husband said that they are perfect as they are.
I followed the recipe except I used fresh blueberries. Maybe I'd put in a few more berries next time and maybe substitute the 1/4 cup all-purpose with whole wheat flour to make it healthier.

Great recipe for breakfast or brunch! Some muffin recipes taste like cake, not this one and only 180 calories each. I used almond milk instead of whole milk and added extra fresh raspberries. I would make this recipe again.

As some previous reviewers, I used 1/4 c of cooking oil & 1/4 c of applesauce plus 1 tsp of vanilla with 1 c more of blueberries. It could do with a bit more brown sugar. I too, had the cupcake paper stick to the muffin. Other than those minor things, I really like the taste & texture. Easy to make.

These had a very good flavor, but I used frozen blueberries and they were too wet. It made the muffins fall apart. Didn't affect the flavor, but they were messy to eat. Also, I wanted to give some to a neighbor and I had to choose from the few that stayed together. I would make again, but probably stick with fresh berries.
Made as directed with fresh berries. Only used half the butter though. Good texture and just the right amount of sweetnes. Hubs are 3 in one sitying! So I'd say they are a hit.

This is our favorite blueberry muffins recipe! We swap 1/4 cup canola oil for half of the melted butter and often reduce sugar, but I almost always reduce sugar when I bake. This is fine with frozen berries if you thaw them out and drain the juice before adding them in. I love baking with cornmeal. Thanks for this great recipe!
